title: A 0.1% allowance admitted exponential fits for 471 of 477 falling Arctic winter line windows in 1980-2011
abstract: We tested whether exact straight daily flow segments can also fit a single exponential with small bounded error. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 at Ob, Lena, Yenisey and Mackenzie in 30 common certified years from 1980 to 2011. Of 477 falling seven-point winter windows, 471 (98.74%) admit a fit within a multiplicative factor of 1.001 at every point. Of 130 maximal falling runs, 122 (93.85%) meet the same bound. An endpoint-chord formula gives the exact minimum uniform log error. Independent numerical fits and a scalar audit checked the calculation. A synthetic rounded exponential also passes the straight-line detector. The result limits interpretation of short exact lines when small time-varying errors are allowed. It does not identify actual rounding, interpolation or natural drainage. Error allowances are chosen, each segment has its own fit, and source processing labels are absent. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, audits and a figure support reproduction. Raw records and derived segment tables remain external.

display.caption: Minimum log errors for winter line segments. The vertical line marks a factor of 1.001. These are fixed-record compatibility fractions, not probabilities of natural drainage.
